chapters.title: Information & Communication Technology: World & Bangladesh Perspective

content.overview: Information and communication technology has transformed human society into a global village. Key concepts include virtual reality, biometric authentication, robotics, cryosurgery, artificial intelligence, genetic engineering, nanotechnology, and cyber ethics.
key_terms: Global Village: Marshall McLuhan's concept of interconnected world through media and telecommunication.
Virtual Reality (VR): Computer-simulated 3D environment giving sensory immersion.
Biometrics: Automated identification of individuals based on physiological or behavioural traits.
Cryosurgery: The use of extreme sub-zero cold to destroy abnormal or diseased tissue (e.g., using liquid nitrogen).
Nanotechnology: Manipulation of matter on an atomic, molecular, and supramolecular scale (1 to 100 nm).
study_notes: Liquid nitrogen (-196°C) and liquid argon are commonly used cryogens in cryosurgery.
DNA profiling and fingerprinting provide the highest accuracy in biometric identification.
Genetic engineering involves recombinant DNA technology.

mcqs.content: Who is credited with originating the term 'Global Village'? A. Charles Babbage B. Marshall McLuhan C. Tim Berners-Lee D. Alan Turing Answer: B
Which substance is most commonly used in cryosurgery as a cooling agent? A. Liquid oxygen B. Liquid nitrogen C. Liquid helium D. Dry ice Answer: B
What is the primary technology used to create interactive 3D simulated environments? A. Artificial Intelligence B. Virtual Reality C. Nanotechnology D. Biometrics Answer: B
Which biometric technique relies on behavioral characteristics rather than physiological traits? A. Fingerprint scanning B. Iris recognition C. Keystroke dynamics D. Facial recognition Answer: C
Nanotechnology deals with structures having dimensions in what range? A. 1 to 100 micrometers B. 1 to 100 nanometers C. 100 to 1000 nanometers D. Above 1 millimeter Answer: B
Recombinant DNA technology is primarily a tool of which scientific discipline? A. Nanotechnology B. Genetic engineering C. Robotics D. Telecommunications Answer: B
The ethical and legal protection of software creator's intellectual property is known as: A. Open Source B. Copyright C. Freeware D. Shareware Answer: B
Which sensor in a smartphone detects screen rotation and device orientation? A. Proximity sensor B. Accelerometer / Gyroscope C. Ambient light sensor D. Barometer Answer: B
What is the main advantage of tele-medicine for rural Bangladesh? A. Low hardware cost B. Remote healthcare access C. Free medication D. Faster internet Answer: B
The concept of sending unsolicited bulk messages over email is known as: A. Phishing B. Spamming C. Spoofing D. Hacking Answer: B
Which biometric system is considered most unique and stable across an individual's lifetime? A. Voice print B. Iris recognition C. Signature verification D. Hand geometry Answer: B
The technology that enables computer software to perform tasks requiring human cognition is: A. Cloud Computing B. Artificial Intelligence C. Big Data D. IoT Answer: B
Which programming language is predominantly used in AI expert systems? A. Fortran B. Prolog & Lisp C. COBOL D. Pascal Answer: B
What type of surgery minimizes blood loss by freezing tissue cells? A. Laparoscopy B. Cryosurgery C. Angioplasty D. Endoscopy Answer: B
In biotechnology, GMO stands for: A. General Mutant Organism B. Genetically Modified Organism C. Global Molecular Order D. Guided Microbial Origin Answer: B
Which is an example of an on-demand computing model accessible via the internet? A. Local Server B. Cloud Computing C. Offline Network D. Standalone PC Answer: B
Unauthorized intrusion into a computer network with malicious intent is termed: A. White-hat hacking B. Cracking / Black-hat hacking C. Data recovery D. Firewalling Answer: B
What is the primary medium used in modern telepresence conferencing? A. Radio waves B. High-speed broadband fiber optics C. Copper wires D. Satellite only Answer: B
Which organization manages and allocates top-level domain names globally? A. IEEE B. ICANN C. W3C D. ISO Answer: B
Which generation of mobile technology introduced massive IoT and ultra-low latency? A. 3G B. 4G C. 5G D. 2G Answer: C

content.answer_tip: Focus on the physical principles of cryogens, unit dimensions of nano, and distinctive biometric traits.

content.overview: Data communication transmits digital or analog signals between nodes across physical or wireless media. Encompasses transmission modes, guided media (coaxial, twisted pair, optical fiber), unguided media (radio, microwave, infrared), network topologies, and cloud infrastructure.
key_terms: Bandwidth: The data transmission capacity of a communication channel, measured in bps.
Simplex, Half-Duplex, Full-Duplex: Transmission directions (one-way, alternate two-way, simultaneous two-way).
Optical Fiber: Glass or plastic core transmitting light signals using Total Internal Reflection (TIR).
Network Topology: Geometric arrangement of computing devices (Star, Bus, Ring, Mesh, Tree, Hybrid).
Cloud Computing: Scalable on-demand delivery of computing services (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS).
study_notes: Optical fiber consists of core, cladding, and buffer coating. Cladding refractive index is strictly lower than core.
Star topology relies on a central hub/switch; failure of the hub halts network communication.
Bluetooth standard is IEEE 802.15.1; Wi-Fi is IEEE 802.11; WiMAX is IEEE 802.16.

mcqs.content: Which physical principle governs light propagation through optical fiber core? A. Refraction B. Total Internal Reflection C. Diffraction D. Dispersion Answer: B
In which transmission mode can both sender and receiver transmit data simultaneously? A. Simplex B. Half-duplex C. Full-duplex D. Synchronous Answer: C
A walkie-talkie communication channel is an example of which mode? A. Simplex B. Half-duplex C. Full-duplex D. Broadcast Answer: B
Which network topology uses a central hub or switch to connect all nodes? A. Bus B. Ring C. Star D. Mesh Answer: C
Which wireless standard operates under IEEE 802.11? A. Bluetooth B. Wi-Fi C. WiMAX D. ZigBee Answer: B
What is the standard IEEE specification for Bluetooth technology? A. IEEE 802.3 B. IEEE 802.11 C. IEEE 802.15.1 D. IEEE 802.16 Answer: C
Which transmission medium provides the highest data transmission speed and immunity to EMI? A. Coaxial cable B. Shielded twisted pair C. Optical fiber D. Unshielded twisted pair Answer: C
In optical fiber, the refractive index of the cladding is: A. Higher than the core B. Lower than the core C. Equal to the core D. Zero Answer: B
Which network topology connects every computer directly to every other computer? A. Bus B. Star C. Ring D. Complete Mesh Answer: D
How many point-to-point physical links are required in a fully connected mesh network of n nodes? A. n B. n - 1 C. n(n - 1) / 2 D. n^2 Answer: C
Which device directs data packets across multiple networks based on IP addresses? A. Switch B. Hub C. Router D. Repeater Answer: C
Which connector type is standard for terminating unshielded twisted pair (UTP) Ethernet cables? A. BNC B. RJ-45 C. SC D. USB Answer: B
Geostationary satellites are placed at approximately what altitude above the Earth's equator? A. 2,000 km B. 10,000 km C. 36,000 km D. 100,000 km Answer: C
Microwave signals require which transmission path property? A. Line-of-Sight (LoS) B. Sky wave propagation C. Ground wave reflection D. Subsea guidance Answer: A
Which cloud computing model delivers ready-to-use software applications over the internet (e.g., Google Workspace)? A. IaaS B. PaaS C. SaaS D. DaaS Answer: C
Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for end-to-end reliability and flow control? A. Physical B. Data Link C. Network D. Transport Answer: D
What is the typical bandwidth range of Voiceband telephone channels? A. 300 to 3400 Hz B. 10 to 50 kHz C. 1 to 5 MHz D. 1 GHz Answer: A
Which wireless communication technology is used for short distances (under 1 meter) in TV remotes? A. Radio waves B. Microwave C. Infrared D. Satellite Answer: C
What happens in a bus topology when the main backbone cable breaks? A. Only one node fails B. The entire network collapses C. Speed increases D. It switches to ring Answer: B
Which IPv4 address class provides the largest number of host addresses per network ID? A. Class A B. Class B C. Class C D. Class D Answer: A

content.answer_tip: Remember TIR requirements, topology formulas n(n-1)/2, and standard IEEE protocols.

content.overview: Explores positional number systems (Binary, Octal, Decimal, Hexadecimal), base conversions, 2's complement arithmetic, boolean algebra, logic gates, De Morgan's theorems, encoders, decoders, and binary adders.
key_terms: Positional Number System: Base-b system where digit value depends on position (powers of b).
2's Complement: 1's complement + 1, used for negative number representation and subtraction via addition.
Universal Gates: NAND and NOR gates, from which all other basic logic gates can be constructed.
Encoder: Combinational circuit converting 2^n inputs into n binary outputs.
Decoder: Combinational circuit decoding n binary inputs into 2^n unique outputs.
study_notes: 2's complement of an 8-bit number: Invert all bits and add 1.
XOR gate outputs 1 if and only if the inputs are different (odd parity).
Half adder outputs: Sum = A XOR B, Carry = A AND B.

mcqs.content: What is the equivalent hexadecimal representation of binary (11011010)_2? A. DA_16 B. DB_16 C. AC_16 D. CB_16 Answer: A
What is the base or radix of the Octal number system? A. 2 B. 8 C. 10 D. 16 Answer: B
Which pair of logic gates are known as Universal Gates? A. AND & OR B. NAND & NOR C. XOR & XNOR D. NOT & AND Answer: B
In boolean algebra, what does the expression (A + A') evaluate to? A. 0 B. 1 C. A D. A' Answer: B
How is the 2's complement of a binary number obtained? A. Invert all bits B. Invert all bits and add 1 C. Add 1 then invert D. Double the number Answer: B
What is the output boolean equation for the Sum (S) in a Half Adder circuit? A. A AND B B. A OR B C. A XOR B D. A XNOR B Answer: C
What is the output boolean equation for the Carry (C) in a Half Adder circuit? A. A AND B B. A OR B C. A XOR B D. NOT A Answer: A
How many Half Adders and OR gates are required to construct one Full Adder? A. 1 Half Adder + 2 OR gates B. 2 Half Adders + 1 OR gate C. 3 Half Adders D. 2 Half Adders + 2 OR gates Answer: B
A digital circuit with 8 inputs that produces 3 binary output lines is called a: A. Decoder B. 8-to-3 Encoder C. Multiplexer D. Flip-flop Answer: B
According to De Morgan's first theorem, (A + B)' is equivalent to: A. A' + B' B. A' . B' C. A . B D. (A . B)' Answer: B
What is the decimal equivalent of the octal number (17)_8? A. 15 B. 17 C. 25 D. 12 Answer: A
Which logic gate gives output 0 only when all inputs are 1? A. AND B. NAND C. OR D. NOR Answer: B
The number of bits required to encode one hexadecimal digit is: A. 2 bits B. 3 bits C. 4 bits D. 8 bits Answer: C
What is the result of adding binary (101)_2 and (011)_2? A. (1000)_2 B. (110)_2 C. (111)_2 D. (1001)_2 Answer: A
In 8-bit sign-magnitude representation, what does the leftmost bit indicate? A. Parity B. Sign (0 for positive, 1 for negative) C. Magnitude D. Base Answer: B
What is the binary representation of decimal 25? A. (11001)_2 B. (11010)_2 C. (10101)_2 D. (11100)_2 Answer: A
What is the output of an XOR gate when both inputs are 1? A. 1 B. 0 C. High impedance D. Undefined Answer: B
Which circuit is commonly used to display numerical values on a 7-segment LED display? A. BCD to 7-segment decoder B. Priority Encoder C. Full Adder D. Comparator Answer: A
What is the 1's complement of binary (101100)_2? A. (010011)_2 B. (010100)_2 C. (110011)_2 D. (010010)_2 Answer: A
In boolean algebra, what does (A . A) simplify to? A. 1 B. 0 C. A D. 2A Answer: C

content.answer_tip: Review 2's complement subtraction steps and memorize half-adder boolean equations (Sum=XOR, Carry=AND).

content.overview: HTML is the standard markup language for creating webpages. Covers URL structure, web domain, IP addressing, HTTP protocol, HTML structural tags, tables, hyperlinks, image integration, and list creation.
key_terms: HTML: HyperText Markup Language, the standard code structure of the World Wide Web.
URL: Uniform Resource Locator, web address specifying protocol, domain, and path.
Hyperlink: Clickable link created with the <a> tag using the href attribute.
HTML Table: Structured data container using <table>, <tr>, <th>, and <td> tags.
study_notes: The tag is an empty/void tag that requires the 'src' and 'alt' attributes.
Ordered lists use <ol> and unordered lists use <ul>; list items use <li>.
Table cells are spanned using 'colspan' and 'rowspan' attributes.

mcqs.content: Which HTML tag is used to create a hyperlink to another webpage? A. <link> B. <href> C. <a> D. <hyperlink> Answer: C
Which attribute of the tag specifies the image source file path? A. link B. src C. href D. path Answer: B
What tag is used to create a standard data cell in an HTML table? A. <th> B. <td> C. <tr> D. <tc> Answer: B
Which HTML tag defines the largest heading size? A. <h6> B. <head> C. <h1> D. <header> Answer: C
Which attribute is used to merge multiple columns in an HTML table? A. rowspan B. colspan C. merge-col D. span Answer: B
Which tag generates an unordered (bulleted) list in HTML? A. <ol> B. <ul> C. <li> D. <list> Answer: B

What type of tag is the
tag in HTML? A. Paired container tag B. Empty / Void tag C. Structural header tag D. Deprecated tag Answer: B
What is the default port number used by the unencrypted HTTP protocol? A. 21 B. 25 C. 80 D. 443 Answer: C
Which protocol provides secure encrypted transmission over the web? A. FTP B. HTTP C. HTTPS D. SMTP Answer: C
In a website architecture, what is the initial landing page typically named? A. main.html B. index.html C. home.html D. default.html Answer: B
Which tag contains visible document contents rendered by web browsers? A. <head> B. <title> C. <body> D. <meta> Answer: C
What is the correct HTML entity for creating a non-breaking space? A. &space; B.   C. ␣ D. &sp; Answer: B
Which attribute specifies alternative text when an image fails to load? A. title B. alt C. desc D. name Answer: B
What is the purpose of the <title> tag inside the <head> element? A. Shows big title on page B. Sets browser tab title C. Formats text D. Creates H1 heading Answer: B
Which website structure allows visitors to browse pages linearly step-by-step? A. Tree / Hierarchical B. Linear / Sequential C. Webbed / Mesh D. Hybrid Answer: B
Which tag is used to format text with italics in modern HTML? A. <i> or <em> B. <italic> C. <it> D. <slant> Answer: A
The process of uploading website files to an online web server is known as: A. Web Hosting B. Web Browsing C. Domain Registration D. Routing Answer: A
What does CSS stand for in web development? A. Creative Style Sheets B. Cascading Style Sheets C. Computer Style Systems D. Colorful Site Styles Answer: B
Which attribute opens a hyperlink in a brand new browser tab? A. target='_blank' B. new='true' C. window='new' D. open='tab' Answer: A
Which organization develops interoperable web standards including HTML and CSS? A. IEEE B. W3C C. ISO D. ANSI Answer: B

content.answer_tip:
Keep in mind void tags like
and do not require closing tags.

content.overview: Introduction to computer programming, generations of programming languages, translator programs (compiler, interpreter, assembler), algorithms, flowcharts, and ANSI C programming syntax, operators, loops, arrays, and functions.
key_terms: Compiler: Translates entire source code into machine code in a single execution pass.
Interpreter: Translates and executes source code line-by-line.
Algorithm & Flowchart: Step-by-step logical solution and its graphical schematic representation.
C Data Types: int, float, double, char, void.
Loop Constructs: for, while, and do-while loops.
study_notes: Every standard C program execution begins inside the main() function.
Format specifiers: %d for int, %f for float, %lf for double, %c for char, %s for string.
do-while loop is an exit-controlled loop; it executes at least once even if the condition is false.

mcqs.content: Who is the creator of the C programming language at Bell Labs? A. Bjarne Stroustrup B. Dennis Ritchie C. James Gosling D. Guido van Rossum Answer: B
Which symbol represents a Decision / Condition step in a standard flowchart? A. Rectangle B. Parallelogram C. Diamond / Rhombus D. Oval Answer: C
What shape represents Input / Output operations in a standard flowchart? A. Rectangle B. Parallelogram C. Diamond D. Circle Answer: B
Which translator converts assembly language mnemonics into machine code? A. Compiler B. Interpreter C. Assembler D. Linker Answer: C
Which format specifier is used in printf() to display a floating-point number? A. %d B. %c C. %f D. %s Answer: C
What is the standard size of an int data type on standard 32-bit/64-bit systems? A. 1 byte B. 4 bytes C. 8 bytes D. 16 bytes Answer: B
Which loop in C is guaranteed to execute its body at least once? A. for B. while C. do-while D. nested-for Answer: C
Which operator in C returns the remainder after integer division? A. / B. % C. & D. ^ Answer: B
Which statement immediately terminates the innermost enclosing loop or switch? A. continue B. break C. return D. exit Answer: B
What is the index of the first element in a standard C array of size 10? A. 1 B. 0 C. -1 D. 10 Answer: B
What character is used to terminate every C statement? A. Colon (:) B. Semicolon (;) C. Period (.) D. Comma (,) Answer: B
Which header file is required to use printf() and scanf() in C? A. <math.h> B. <stdio.h> C. <stdlib.h> D. <string.h> Answer: B
What is the value of the boolean expression (5 > 3 && 2 > 4) in C? A. 1 (true) B. 0 (false) C. -1 D. Error Answer: B
In C, what is the pre-increment expression ++x equivalent to? A. x = x + 1 before evaluation B. x = x + 1 after evaluation C. x = x * 2 D. x unchanged Answer: A
Which of the following is an invalid C variable identifier name? A. student_1 B. _count C. 2total D. sumTotal Answer: C
What is the null character terminating standard strings in C? A. '\0' B. '\n' C. '\t' D. 'EOF' Answer: A
Which language generation (GL) does C belong to? A. 1GL (Machine) B. 2GL (Assembly) C. 3GL (High-Level Procedural) D. 4GL Answer: C
What does the continue statement do in a C loop? A. Terminates loop B. Skips remaining body of current iteration C. Exits program D. Restarts main Answer: B
Which function is used to take formatted input from the user keyboard in C? A. print() B. scanf() C. read() D. cin>> Answer: B
What is the return type of a function that does not return any value? A. int B. null C. void D. empty Answer: C

content.answer_tip: Remember flowchart symbols (Diamond=Decision, Parallelogram=I/O) and C operator precedence.

content.overview: DBMS provides efficient data storage, retrieval, and manipulation. Topics include Relational Database Management Systems (RDBMS), primary keys, foreign keys, relationships, SQL commands, indexing, and data security.
key_terms: Primary Key: A unique attribute that unequivocally identifies each record/tuple in a table.
Foreign Key: An attribute in one table referencing the Primary Key of another table, establishing a relationship.
SQL (Structured Query Language): Standard language for interacting with relational databases.
Tuple & Field: A row representing a single entity record, and a column representing an attribute.
study_notes: A Primary Key field cannot contain duplicate values and cannot be NULL.
SQL clauses: SELECT extracts data, WHERE filters, ORDER BY sorts, UPDATE modifies, DELETE removes.

mcqs.content: In a relational database table, what does each row (tuple) represent? A. An attribute B. A single record C. A data type D. An index Answer: B
Which characteristic is strictly required for a Primary Key field? A. Must be numbers B. Unique and not null C. Auto-incrementing D. Uppercase Answer: B
What is an attribute in a table that references the primary key of another table called? A. Candidate key B. Foreign key C. Composite key D. Alternate key Answer: B
Which SQL command is used to extract data from a relational database table? A. GET B. SELECT C. EXTRACT D. OPEN Answer: B
Which SQL clause is used to filter records meeting a specific condition? A. GROUP BY B. WHERE C. ORDER BY D. HAVING Answer: B
What does the SQL command 'DELETE FROM students;' do? A. Deletes the table structure B. Deletes all rows in the table C. Drops database D. Clears index Answer: B
What relationship exists between a student and their unique Student ID registration? A. One-to-Many B. Many-to-Many C. One-to-One D. Many-to-One Answer: C
What relationship exists between a Teacher and the multiple Courses they teach? A. One-to-One B. One-to-Many C. Many-to-One D. Independent Answer: B
What technique is used in DBMS to significantly accelerate data search queries? A. Encryption B. Indexing C. Compression D. Normalization Answer: B
The process of organizing data to reduce data redundancy and eliminate anomalies is: A. Normalization B. Backup C. Denormalization D. Clustering Answer: A
Which data type is best suited to store student names up to 50 characters? A. INTEGER B. VARCHAR / TEXT C. BOOLEAN D. DATE Answer: B
Which SQL keyword is used to sort the resulting query dataset? A. SORT BY B. ORDER BY C. ALIGN BY D. ARRANGE Answer: B
Which SQL aggregate function counts the total number of rows matching a criteria? A. SUM() B. COUNT() C. TOTAL() D. AVG() Answer: B
What does DDL stand for in SQL database architecture? A. Data Definition Language B. Data Description Logic C. Database Delivery Link D. Direct Data Link Answer: A
Which of the following SQL statements is a Data Manipulation Language (DML) command? A. CREATE B. DROP C. INSERT D. ALTER Answer: C
What occurs when the same data is unnecessarily duplicated in multiple tables? A. Data integrity B. Data redundancy C. Data security D. Data isolation Answer: B
A key composed of two or more attributes to uniquely identify a record is called a: A. Simple key B. Composite primary key C. Foreign key D. Super key Answer: B
Which SQL clause groups rows that have the same values in specified columns? A. ORDER BY B. GROUP BY C. MERGE D. JOIN Answer: B
In MS Access or relational tables, a column is also referred to as a: A. Tuple B. Field / Attribute C. Domain D. Sheet Answer: B

Which property guarantees database transactions are processed reliably (ACID)? A. Accuracy, Control, Identity, Data B. Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability C. Access, Compute, Index, Deploy D. Asynchronous, Clean, Integrated, Distributed Answer: B

content.answer_tip: Remember Primary key cannot be null, Foreign key enables relationships, and ACID principles.
